description: ktor-kronos — JetBrains Ktor on Kotlin/Native with the kron engine (ktor-server-kron, in the MDA2AV/ktor fork) instead of CIO. kron is the native port of the ioxide io_uring runtime: one reactor per core, each pinned to its CPU and owning its ring and its share of the SO_REUSEPORT listeners; multishot accept and recv into provided buffer rings, driven from Kotlin over the kernel's own io_uring header (no liburing, no JVM: one native binary). Requests are parsed by Glyph11, the hardened HTTP/1.1 parser, and run through Ktor's own pipeline - routing, plugins, call.receive and call.respond - on the reactor that accepted the connection, with no thread pool in between. Responses to pipelined requests leave in one send. delay() is an IORING_OP_TIMEOUT on the reactor's ring, so a held connection in the async profile costs a kernel deadline rather than a timer thread. WebSockets are Ktor's own, over the upgraded connection. The routes are the ktor entry's, answered the same way; only the engine and the platform differ. The engine passes Ktor's own engine suites (HttpServerCommonTestSuite, WebSocketEngineSuite). TLS on :8081 is the engine's own connector on kron's BoringSSL, the kernel encrypting the records (kTLS TX) where it has the tls module. JSON is Ktor's ContentNegotiation with kotlinx.serialization, gzipped by Ktor's own Compression plugin, which the fork brings to Kotlin/Native on zlib.
